one_liner: Protobuf codec generated as AssemblyScript classes inside WebAssembly; encodes about 2.2x faster than protobuf.js but decodes slower.
what_it_does: Two npm packages: as-proto-gen is a protoc plugin (protoc --plugin=protoc-gen-as=... --as_out=.) that emits one AssemblyScript file per message and enum with static encode(message, writer) and decode(reader, length) methods, plus optional encodeX/decodeX helpers (--as_opt=gen-helper-methods); as-proto is the runtime (Protobuf.encode/decode, Writer, Reader). Messages are AssemblyScript objects in wasm linear memory, so it serves code written in AssemblyScript, not JavaScript callers. It handles plain messages, maps and imported dependencies; gRPC service definitions are not supported.
how_it_is_fast: Encoding is two-pass: a FixedSizer walks the message once, recording the total length and every nested-message and string length in a varlen array, then FixedWriter allocates one exactly sized Uint8Array and writes varints and fixed-width fields with direct store<T> calls, taking each length prefix from the precomputed array, so nothing is backpatched or concatenated (protobuf.js instead builds a linked list of write ops and joins it in finish()). The generated code is monomorphic static calls on typed fields (u32, i64, f64) compiled ahead of time by asc at optimizeLevel 3 with @inline varint helpers and global reused WRITER/READER instances. Decoding allocates AssemblyScript objects, arrays and strings on its incremental GC heap, which the author blames for the decode loss.
when_to_use: An AssemblyScript wasm module (plugin, edge worker, contract or guest) that must encode or decode protobuf itself without calling back into JavaScript.
Encode-heavy paths with small messages of mostly scalar fields: the author's run shows 1.30M vs 0.59M ops/s for protobuf.js on one small message.
Both ends are as-proto, or the peer accepts unpacked repeated scalars (as-proto writes proto3 repeated scalars unpacked unless [packed=true] is set).
Messages that hold only primitives and nested messages, the case where the README says decoding also beats JavaScript.
when_not_to_use: JavaScript or TypeScript application code: the benchmark never crosses the JS-wasm boundary, and in real use every message would have to be marshalled into and out of wasm memory; use protobuf.js there.
Decode-heavy workloads with strings and repeated fields: protobuf.js decoded 1.38M ops/s against as-proto's 0.89M on the author's run.

Reading proto3 data from other encoders: proto3 packs repeated scalars by default, but the generator emits the packed decode path only for an explicit [packed=true], so packed data from protobuf.js, google-protobuf or C++ is misread (issue #55; fix PR #56 unmerged).
Schemas that need oneof (issue #42 open), gRPC services, or reliable cross-package and well-known-type imports (issues #29, #30, #51 open).
int64/uint64/sint64 fields whose values fall just under a varint byte boundary (see gotchas), or any project that needs an actively maintained codec.

integration.form: module (npm source packages: as-proto runtime compiled into your wasm, as-proto-gen protoc plugin)
integration.dependencies: protoc for code generation; the AssemblyScript compiler (asc); Node.js 10.4+ or a browser with WebAssembly at runtime
integration.min_toolchain: AssemblyScript 0.23+ (CHANGELOG v0.6.0; the repo pins ^0.24.1); newer asc releases not documented; protoc 3.x (generated headers show 3.20.3 and 3.21.4)
integration.platforms: any WebAssembly host that runs asc output (Node.js, browsers, standalone wasm runtimes)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; Protobuf.encode and decode use global WRITER and READER singletons, so calls are not reentrant and are unsafe across shared-memory wasm threads.

gotchas: Benchmark correctness: the README numbers date from the initial commit (a70d19f, 2022-01-04, asc ^0.19.20, release target with converge false) and were never re-run. In that code the generated packed-repeated decoder computed its end as reader.ptr + reader.uint32(), reading ptr before the length varint, so (simulating the 80 encoded bytes) the bench decode stopped one bool early, read the 7th bool byte as a fixed64 tag, skipped the double and the outer float field, and read one byte past the buffer with bounds checks stripped by noAssert. Results were discarded, so the decoding and combined rows time an incorrect decode; the encode row produced correct bytes.

The same reader.ptr + reader.uint32() end is still on main in the explicit-packed and map-entry decoders, and proto3 default-packed repeated scalars are not recognized at all; issue #55 and fix PR #56 have been open since 2026-02-19.

FixedSizer.varint64 uses half the correct limits for 5- to 9-byte varints, so 64-bit values in [2^34,2^35), [2^41,2^42), [2^48,2^49), [2^55,2^56) and [2^62,2^63) are sized one byte too long: nested length prefixes overstate by one and the top-level buffer gets a trailing zero byte (an invalid tag 0). Fix PR #57 is unmerged.

Before v1.2.1 (2023-03-24) the generator marked primitive-only messages @unmanaged, which leaked one object per decode (issue #47); the benchmark's InnerInner was such a class when the README numbers were taken. Release builds with noAssert also remove FixedReader's bounds checks, so truncated or hostile input is read out of bounds silently.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only protobuf codec in this category; pick it over json-as when an AssemblyScript module must speak protobuf rather than JSON, and accept that you are adopting a stale codebase with open decoder bugs.
verified_claims_summary: On a 2015 MacBook Pro (Core i7 2.2 GHz, Node.js version not stated), ts-proto's benchmark.js suite with an added as-proto case encoded one small Test message at 1.30M ops/s inside wasm (asc 0.19-era build, optimizeLevel 3, incremental runtime, noAssert) vs 0.59M for protobuf.js static and reflect (2.2x), decoded at 0.89M vs 1.38M (1.5x slower) and ran encode plus decode at 0.55M vs 0.44M (1.25x). The as-proto rows reuse a message pre-built in wasm and never cross into JavaScript, the payload values differ slightly from protobuf.js's, and the decode and combined rows ran a decoder that misparsed the message's packed bool field.
status_note: Stale since 2023-03-24 (npm as-proto 1.3.0, MIT, small enough to vendor), with three community fix PRs (#56 packed decoding, #57 varint64 sizer, #58 tests) unmerged since February 2026; the record's compiler_and_flags (asc ^0.24.1, converge true) describe today's bench script, not the 2022 build behind the numbers, whose decode and combined rows timed an incorrect decode and should not be relied on.
